items.prompt: Black's third move was ...Qh4, an early queen sortie. Ask the three questions (what did it change, what does it threaten, what can you do about it?), then play your move.

claims.statement: Nxh4 is the engine's best move.
Nxh4 wins the queen for nothing.

hints: What did the queen move change? Look at which squares your knight covers.
The queen threatens e4 and f2, but ask first whether it can be taken.
Your knight on f3 attacks h4.
items.explain: The queen came out early onto a square the knight on f3 attacks. Nothing needs defending first: you simply take it. Checked: Nxh4 is the engine's top move and wins the queen.

feedback_by_move.c4f7: Bxf7+ is tempting but it gives up the chance to win the queen outright; Nxh4 is far stronger.

items.prompt: Black answered the knight sortie with ...Nxe4 instead of the usual defences. Ask the three questions, then choose your move.

claims.statement: Bxf7+ is the engine's best move.
Nxe4 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.
Nf3 is at least 100 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: What did the knight capture leave undefended near the black king?
Your bishop and knight both aim at f7.
One of the two captures on f7 comes with check and wins material.
items.explain: Black's knight took the centre pawn but left the king with only one guard on f7. Bxf7+ comes with check and the engine rates it clearly best; recapturing on e4 or retreating both lose ground.

feedback_by_move.g5e4: Nxe4 regains the pawn but lets Black off lightly; the engine rates it well below Bxf7+.
feedback_by_move.g5f3: Retreating throws away the chance Black's move gave you.

items.prompt: Black developed the bishop with ...Bg4, pinning your knight to the queen, and left the e5 pawn under attack. Ask the three questions, then play your move.

claims.statement: dxe5, Be3 and Nc3 are all within 40 centipawns of the best move.

hints: What does the bishop on g4 attack, and what does the pawn on d6 no longer guard?
Nothing of yours is hanging; you may develop or take in the centre.
A capture on e5, or a developing move.
items.explain: The pin on f3 is not a real threat yet, so you can follow your opening habits. The engine puts dxe5, Be3 and Nc3 within 40 centipawns of one another.

items.prompt: Black has played a Scandinavian: queen out early, then ...Bg4. White to move. Ask the three questions, then pick a developing move.

claims.statement: h3, Bd2 and Bc4 are all within 40 centipawns of the best move.

hints: The queen was chased once already. Where are Black's pieces aiming now?
Black's bishop pins your knight. You can ask it a question or simply develop.
h3, Bd2 and Bc4 all keep the advantage.
items.explain: Black has spent time on the queen. White keeps the lead by asking the bishop a question or developing with tempo; the engine puts h3, Bd2 and Bc4 within 40 centipawns.

items.prompt: A French Winawer, where Black has just castled while your queen sits on g4. What does Black's last move change, and what does it threaten? Then choose.

claims.statement: Nf3, Bd3, Qh5 and Qh3 are within 40 centipawns of the best move.

hints: Black's king is now on g8. Does it threaten your queen?
Nothing is attacked; think about development and the safety of your queen.
Develop the knight or bishop, or move the queen to a better post.
items.explain: Castling does not attack anything. White's queen can stay active, and four sensible moves are within 40 centipawns, led by Nf3.

items.prompt: This is a Petroff, but Black grabbed the e4 pawn at once with ...Nxe4. What did that move change, and what does it leave unprotected? Choose your move.

claims.statement: Qe2 is the engine's best move.
Be2 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Which Black pieces now guard the knight on e4?
The queen on e2 attacks the knight and prepares a trick on the e-file.
Qe2 threatens to win a piece.
items.explain: The knight on e4 is held only by tactics. Qe2 attacks it and sets a trap (if the knight retreats to f6, Nc6+ wins the queen). Checked: Qe2 is the top move; Be2 is worse.

feedback_by_move.f1e2: Be2 lets Black off the hook: it is at least 40 centipawns worse than Qe2.

items.prompt: Black's last move was ...d5. White to move: what did it change, what does it threaten, and which plan fits? Then choose.

claims.statement: e3 and cxd5 are within 40 centipawns of the best move.

hints: Look at the bishop on h4 and the pawn on d5. What is attacked?
Nothing of yours is loose; the central tension can be released or kept.
Support the centre or take on d5.
items.explain: The centre push attacks nothing but forces a decision about the c4 pawn. The engine puts e3 and cxd5 within 40 centipawns of one another.

items.prompt: A London System where Black is mirroring White's set-up. White to move after ...Bb7. Ask the three questions, then pick a sensible move.

claims.statement: Nxc6, Qf3 and O-O are all within 40 centipawns of the best move.

hints: Which of your pieces are attacked? Count the attackers on e5.
Nothing is loose, so you can simplify, castle or bring the queen out.
Nxc6, Qf3 and O-O are all fine.
items.explain: The position is balanced and quiet: nothing is attacked. Three moves score within 40 centipawns, so the lesson is to check for threats, then pick a reasonable plan.
